$comment: Machine-readable contract for what vstack ships, which install profile puts it where, who owns which settings key, and what verifies all of it. CHECK-TIME ORACLE ONLY: no shipped script reads this file at runtime. install.sh, uninstall.sh, overlay.sh and bin/doctor keep deriving from the filesystem; the gate compares their derivation against this file and fails on disagreement. See design note in docs/ (Brief 1 Phase 6 / Brief 3 Phase 1).

derived_at.head: 8d387cbdaaa935123f87b53ca62f652409c58a34
derived_at.digest_recipe_note: payload_digest hashes the working-tree BYTES of every payload file -- tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored -- together with its executable bit and path, then hashes that listing. Recompute it with `tests/inventory-contract.sh --print-digest` and nothing else: typing a recipe by hand into a shell is a second implementation. This field used to hold the recipe as an executable string that the validator eval'd, on the reasoning that the two could then never disagree. That made the artifact its own oracle -- editing the recipe and the digest together passed while measuring nothing -- and it also hashed index blob ids plus `git status --porcelain`, which names files and status letters but never their contents, so two different unstaged edits to the same path produced the same digest. Both were confirmed by running them.
derived_at.staleness_is_the_signal: This file is a snapshot. When the payload digest no longer matches, the validator regenerates every derived field and diffs. A mismatch is the intended failure, not a maintenance chore: it means a component moved and at least one consumer has not been told.
derived_at.concurrency_warning: Recomputed at c4c2d06 in an isolated detached worktree with a clean status, then confirmed byte-identical against the shared checkout rather than assumed. The recipe includes git status --porcelain, so a value computed while a peer's unrelated payload edit sits uncommitted bakes that edit in and matches nothing afterwards. Any consumer that trusts these numbers without regenerating them is still the defect this file exists to catch.
derived_at.head_note: head names the commit payload_digest was computed FROM, not the commit that carries this file -- the latter cannot be recorded from inside the file, for the same fixed-point reason self_reference_note gives about the digest. As of e5d8857 this field IS validated: tests/inventory-contract.sh requires it to be a 40-character hash and an ancestor of HEAD, reports the distance in commits, and skips (naming the reason) when the commit is absent from the checkout. It fails when the hash exists but is not an ancestor, which is the case where the snapshot was taken on a commit this branch does not descend from.
derived_at.self_reference_note: claude/inventory.json lives inside claude/, which this recipe scans, so the recipe excludes the file's own path with a git pathspec. Without that exclusion the digest could never match itself: committing the file changes its own blob hash, which changes the scanned tree, which changes the digest the file is trying to record -- a fixed point that cannot be reached by editing the file. Excluding the file's own path makes payload_digest mean "did the shippable payload move", not "did this contract about the payload move", which is also the more honest reading of the field's name.
derived_at.computation_discipline: The recipe includes git status --porcelain, so it is sensitive to UNCOMMITTED changes in whatever checkout computes it -- including files this contract does not otherwise care about, as long as they fall under the scanned paths. Computing it in a shared checkout while another agent's unrelated edit (e.g. install.sh) sits uncommitted bakes that edit's presence into payload_digest, producing a value a clean worktree of the same commit will never reproduce. Recompute payload_digest from a clean worktree (git status --porcelain empty) of the commit being recorded, never from a dirty shared checkout.

regeneration.rule: Every list and count below is derived from the tree, never hand-written. A validator regenerates them and diffs.

derivations.skills: for d in claude/skills/*/; do basename "${d%/}"; done
derivations.agents: for f in claude/agents/*.md; do basename "$f" .md; done
derivations.agent_references: for f in claude/agents/reference/*.ref; do basename "$f"; done
derivations.commands: for f in claude/commands/*.md; do basename "$f" .md; done
derivations.hooks: for f in claude/hooks/*.sh; do basename "$f"; done
derivations.wrappers: for f in bin/*; do basename "$f"; done

full.description: git clone + ./install.sh. The only lane that installs hooks at user scope, the CLI wrappers, the shell lane, the MCP merge and the Conductor managed layer.

plugin.entrypoint: claude plugin marketplace add itsvedantkumar/vstack && claude plugin install vstack@vstack
plugin.description: Marketplace lane. plugin source is ./claude, so everything under claude/ that Claude Code auto-discovers ships: skills, agents, commands AND claude/hooks/hooks.json.
plugin.hook_note: This lane DOES wire hooks, via claude/hooks/hooks.json auto-discovery. .claude/verify.sh check 11 asserts the exact event set and check 47 runs each wired script in a sandbox with no ~/.config/agents and no vstack wrappers on PATH. A hook whose only reachable outcome names a command this lane never installs does not belong here.

hook_scripts_deliberately_absent.reason: It refuses to run an untrusted .claude/verify.sh and tells the operator to run `vstack trust`, which only the full install provides. Enforced by check 47.

plugin.profile_env: VSTACK_PROFILE=skills (inject-session-context.sh drops the token/delegation/autonomy policy in this lane)

overlay.description: Commits a project-scope .claude/ into another repo. The only config lane that reaches a cloud sandbox, which has no ~/.claude.
overlay.policy_note: claude/CLAUDE.md ships as .claude/hooks/policy.md, NOT .claude/CLAUDE.md: the latter is project memory and would load the same bytes twice alongside ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

skills.floor_reason: claude/skills/ATTRIBUTION.md states that eighteen of the shipped skills are ported from pstack. A total below eighteen makes that section arithmetically impossible, so 18 is the lowest number at which the shipped documentation is still self-consistent.

agents.floor_reason: nine agent prompts point at claude/agents/reference/ENVIRONMENT.ref (grep -l). Fewer than nine of them means at least one of those referrers was deleted, which is a payload change and not a count drift.

agent_references.floor_reason: nine agent prompts name ENVIRONMENT.ref by path. Zero files here means those pointers resolve to nothing.
agent_references.extension_reason: Claude Code's plugin agent walker recurses into subdirectories and loads every file ending .md, at any depth, as an agent. A reference written as .md would install as a nameless plugin agent (vstack:reference:ENVIRONMENT, description auto-filled 'Agent from vstack plugin') competing for dispatch. .claude/verify.sh check 46 enforces both directions.

commands.floor_reason: README.md's 'Day to day' table names /ship, /review, /team, /doctor by hand, and CLAUDE.md routing names /goal and /commit. All six must exist for the shipped prose to resolve.

hooks.floor_reason: Derived, not literal: the floor is the number of distinct hook scripts install.sh's own jq rebuild program names. Every one of those must exist on disk or the user lane installs a hook command pointing at nothing. Recomputed from install.sh on every validation, so it cannot go stale.
hooks.user_lane_exempt_rule: A hook that ships to the plugin lane only must be named here with a one-line reason. Empty today: installing vstack for real use is what install.sh does, so every shipped hook belongs in the user lane. Mirrors USER_LANE_EXEMPT in .claude/verify.sh check 11.

wrappers.floor_reason: bin/doctor asserts four wrappers by name (claude-bg.sh, claude-task.sh, cloudflare-mcp, deploy-auto.sh). Below that, doctor fails anyway; the floor makes the failure name the cause instead of the symptom.
wrappers.not_named_reason: bin/doctor is the checker itself and bin/vstack is the CLI that invokes it; both are covered by --drift's bin/* sweep.

mcp_servers.floor_reason: bin/doctor iterates the keys of mcp/servers.json and reports success when the loop body never runs. One key is the minimum at which that loop measures anything.

settings.retired_rule: A key may enter RETIRED (install.sh) only if claude/settings.json shipped it at some commit and does not ship it now. Enforced by .claude/verify.sh check 21. Deleting a key vstack never shipped is deleting a Claude Code feature on a stranger's machine.
settings.project_scope_rule: overlay.sh may write only these into another repo's committed .claude/settings.json. Source: claude/settings.project-keys. Enforced by .claude/verify.sh check 17.
settings.user_scope_keys_note: bin/doctor carries USER_SCOPE: keys that legitimately exist only on a machine (Claude Code's own, plus per-account state). A live key in neither shipped_keys nor USER_SCOPE is unclassified and doctor --drift reports it.

merge_semantics.top_level: portable file is authoritative for every key it ships; keys it never mentions survive untouched
merge_semantics.hooks: merged by ownership: an entry is vstack's when its command path ends in /hooks/<a filename vstack ships>. Never by directory prefix (a HOME move breaks that) and never by event name (that destroys the user's own hooks).
merge_semantics.skillOverrides: merged, ours win on collision; a stale entry naming no shipped skill is inert
merge_semantics.enabledPlugins: typescript-lsp entry is stripped only when `claude plugin list` does not show it

files.rule: Ownership by receipt first, byte-identity second.
files.receipt: $HOME/.config/agents/vstack-installed — install.sh appends every path it writes; survives a version change, where content comparison cannot.
files.byte_identity_fallback: For a machine with no receipt yet, a target byte-identical to the repo file about to overwrite it is treated as vstack's.
files.stated_trade: A user file whose bytes exactly equal vstack's is indistinguishable from vstack's and is treated as vstack's, so uninstall deletes it. The alternative loses the ability to uninstall at all.
uninstall_rules: a backup holding a prior version wins: restore it
a file edited since install is kept and named, never deleted
only a file still byte-identical to what vstack shipped is removed
symlinks are never touched (builtin and plugin skills link in from elsewhere)
settings.json and .claude.json are unpicked key by key, never deleted

skill_overrides.purpose: Quiet skills that Claude Code and its plugins install on their own. It never parks a skill from this repo. Enforced by .claude/verify.sh check 15.

gate.accounting_rule: ran + skipped must equal declared, or the gate fails. A check wrapped in a conditional with no else reports nothing and used to leave no trace.
gate.offline_reason: The Stop hook runs it on every Stop. Network reachability questions live in bin/doctor instead.

required.note: Mutates the working tree. Run against a throwaway clone. The row total exceeds the declared-check total because some checks can fail in more than one way.

cost_model.note: The slowest falsify shard of that run took 1034s over 16 rows (13 mutation + the 3 fixed rows every shard repeats), 64.6s each, rounded up, with the gate then declaring the number recorded in checks_at_measurement (58). Check 58 of .claude/verify.sh does not hardcode a per-row cost: it scales this measurement by the gate size it finds, because every row runs the WHOLE gate, so adding a check makes every row slower. fixed_seconds is NOT measured and is not claimed to be: one run gives one equation for two unknowns, and the two 16-row shards of that run took 1034s and 690s, so per-row cost varies by row and fixed cost is not separable from it. It is a stated assumption, dominated by the 2x margin check 58 applies. Re-derive seconds_per_row and checks_at_measurement together when re-deriving REQUIRE_CHECKS_WAIT_SECONDS; the query is in the comment beside that value.

required.note: No model calls. Fixture integrity only; it does not prove a skill fires.

optional.why_optional: Billed model calls against a live session; CI has no auth.
Billed model calls; costed suites need an explicit ask.
Needs Docker and network access to published tags.
Needs local stubs for deploy targets.

allowed_skip_reasons.note: NOT allowed for check 0: the toolchain check fails rather than skips, because five checks depend on jq and a partial run must not read as a full pass.
NOT allowed on CI: .github/workflows/verify.yml installs shellcheck and runs `shellcheck --version` so a broken install stops the run.
NOT allowed on ci:verify or ci:install-linux: those jobs install the platform binary on purpose and assert the check did not skip.
A shallow clone has no tags. CI uses fetch-depth: 0 so this must not fire there.

allowed_skip_reasons.reason: declared version is not tagged yet
allowed_skip_reasons.note: Between the version bump and the tag there is no payload to diff against. Tagging restarts the measurement.
Reported as a FAILURE, not a skip: the directory is tracked, so its absence is a defect.

verification.forbidden_skip_rule: A skip is honest only when the missing thing is genuinely not this repo's to supply. A skip on a machine that was set up to run the check is a green measuring nothing, and CI asserts the not-skipped condition explicitly for checks 19 and the marketplace lane.

armed_by: vstack trust [--yes] (any repo, interactive confirmation unless --yes)

inputs.why: the script the Stop hook executes

inputs.what: package.json / pyproject.toml + uv.lock / Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock + build.rs, where the gate reaches for that toolchain
inputs.why: npm run test executes arbitrary script bodies from package.json

trust.rule: The Stop hook refuses to execute a repo's verify.sh unless a machine-local hash entry matches. A bare clone never arms itself. A cloud sandbox arms itself only through a line the operator committed into .conductor/settings.toml, which is the visible consent.

platforms.rule: Support is a claim about what is tested. The runner names in the workflow and the platform names in README.md must be the same set in both directions. Enforced by .claude/verify.sh check 26.
platforms.shell: bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash) is the floor: no mapfile, no declare -A, no sort -V.
platforms.known_non_gnu: BusyBox (Alpine) date, sed, find and stat differ from both BSD and GNU.

measured.rule: A row requires a command or a file that produced the number, and the date it was run.

implemented_unmeasured.rule: The third column is mandatory. A mechanism with no stated unknown belongs in section 1 with evidence, or it is a claim without one.

open_question.rule: Status names the harness that would answer it and its pre-registered floors, or says no harness exists.

run_log.rule: Pin run parameters in the log header. A result produced by uncommitted harness edits is not reproducible.

claims.counts_verified_by: .claude/verify.sh check 12, which derives every count from the tree and reads back every claim in every tracked *.md and *.json outside docs/provenance and docs/research.

known_gaps.what: Check 12 resolves one number per noun for the whole repository. README.md states counts per install lane. The plugin-lane rows happen to equal the full-lane rows for skills, agents and commands today, so the check is satisfied by coincidence rather than by lane.

claude/skills/ATTRIBUTION.md's per-source counts (18/4/1/2/1/2) and its per-source skill name lists are prose. Nothing compares them to the tree or asserts they sum to the skill count. The provenance block in components.skills is the machine-readable form; nothing reads it yet.

docs/what-this-actually-does.md line 25 quotes a run line reading 'checks: 44 declared, 44 ran' as the evidence for a claim whose headline number is the current declared-check total. Check 12 matches the noun but not the bare word 'declared', so the stale measurement is invisible to the gate.

bin/doctor's repo-less fallbacks (HOOKS=, WANT_AGENTS=) name four hook basenames and an agent floor of six, against a tree that ships more of both. They only fire when no vstack repo can be resolved, which is exactly the case with no other source of truth.
uninstall.sh's comment block cites agent, command, hook and wrapper totals that no longer match the tree. Comments are outside check 12's scan of *.md and *.json, so nothing reads them back.

contradictions_resolved_during_this_snap.what: At commit 3f1d020 README.md's plugin-lane table claimed the lane installed no hooks at all and bin/doctor printed 'hooks not part of the plugin lane by design', while claude/hooks/hooks.json wired SessionStart and Stop for that lane and check 11 asserted that exact set. Three of this repository's own artefacts disagreed about whether a shipped component existed in a lane.
contradictions_resolved_during_this_snap.resolution: Fixed in the working tree concurrently with this snapshot: verify-gate.sh removed from the plugin lane, README's row corrected to name the routing hooks it does install, and a check added to run every plugin-lane hook standalone.
contradictions_resolved_during_this_snap.residual: bin/doctor still prints 'hooks not part of the plugin lane by design' at its hooks and secrets branches. Verify before treating this as closed.
